record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Does every effectively compact left-c.e. Polish space have a computable Polish presentation whose metric is right-c.e.?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Does every (effectively) compact left-c.e. Polish space have a computable (right c.e.) Polish copy?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a recent (2025) compilation of open problems from a workshop on computability theory and descriptive set theory. Related separation results are known: there exist left-c.e. Polish spaces with no computable (and no right-c.e.) Polish presentation in general, and every left-c.e. Stone space has a computable Polish copy; but the specific question for effectively compact left-c.e. Polish spaces does not appear to be resolved.

status_evidence.title: Separating notions in effective topology — Melnikov and Ng
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a left-c.e. Polish space not homeomorphic to any right-c.e. space; some left-c.e. spaces have no computable Polish presentation.
status_evidence.claim: Related separation results are known but the compact effectively compact case is not addressed.
